overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights a clear preference for extreme cosmic phenomena, alternative perspective space scenarios ('What If'), and extreme planetary conditions. Videos focused on bizarre planetary extremes and counterintuitive cosmic facts (e.g., Venus day/year anomalies, liquid diamond planets, and absolute darkness) exhibit significantly higher velocity, likes-per-view, and engagement than standard biology or basic psychological facts within the 7-day window.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) achieve top views and highest like ratios within days of publication.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes hypothetical planetary survival and bizarre cosmic anomalies using vivid, high-contrast visual framing.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) demonstrate strong sustained traction over standard informational facts.
winning_patterns.action: Continue utilizing extreme comparative hooks that juxtapose everyday objects or extremes against cosmic phenomena.

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles regarding memory creation (e.g., 5AN7LUgqarc, 2fqaGqfsR4A) and song loops (ef3ND4qiRHc) show stagnant views and low engagement velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard self-help and basic psychology facts in favor of high-visual space and mystery content.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic biology facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) yield lower relative engagement compared to dynamic, cinematic planetary destruction scenarios.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal-related content strictly toward cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies rather than static trivia.
